sections.text: I am all-devouring Death; I am the Origin of all that shall happen; I am Fame, Fortune, Speech, Memory, Intellect, Constancy and Forgiveness.
Of hymns I am Brihatsama, of metres I am Gayatri, among the months I am Margasheersha (December), and I am the Spring among seasons.
I am the Gambling of the cheat and the Splendour of the splendid; I am Victory; I am Effort; and I am the Purity of the pure.

We have been discussing Chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga, Yoga of Divine Glories. As we have seen, Arjuna, after listening to the whole discourse from Bhagavan on the nature of the Supreme self, said, But I need to know more. So in verse 18 he says: Vistarena Atmano Yogam Vibhutim cha Janardana, Bhuyah Kathaya Triptir hi Shrinvato Nasti Me Amritam. Tell me again in detail, O Janardana, your Yoga power and your immanent glory, because I do not feel satisfied hearing your life-giving, nectar-like speech. In other words, he said, give me some examples. So Bhagavan said: Divya hi Atma Vibhutayah , my glories are divine.
Pradhanyataha Kuru Shreshtha Na Astyantah Vistarasya Me. There is no end to this glory, but I can give you some prominent examples. So Bhagavan clearly clarified to Arjuna: Im going to give you some prominent examples.
They do not constitute my entire glory, but they will give you some idea of where to see my presence. So we have been seeing many examples, right from the Vedic period to the Puranic period. And Bhagavan is now even coming down to our day-to-day experiences.
Pavanaha Pavatamasmi , something which we experience in phenomenal nature. Everything and every being is nothing but my own self, because he said everything proceeds from me and I am the source of all things and beings. There is no other thing which has created this universe.
When we see an effect, there have to be two causes. One is the efficient cause , somebody who knows how to make that thing come into existence. And one is the material to create that thing.
Take pizza: we need a pizza maker and pizza ingredients. So if you see pizza here, you cant simply say, Well, the pizza just appeared here. We are Chinmaya Mission, we are divine people.
We dont need to order pizza. Pizza just appears here. We know that an intelligent person will not believe that. He knows that if there is pizza there, there is a pizza maker and he had the ingredients for the pizza.
So the same way, if this world exists, there is the material cause and efficient cause. Material cause is something which we have difficulty understanding. We think if Bhagavan knows everything, obviously he knows how to create this world.
The problem is where did he find the material? How do we create something? Im an architect, so I can create buildings. Because I know how to design building. Just knowing how to create building doesnt create building.
I need to have materials. Go to Home Depot or Lowes to buy that material. Ask Home Depot, Where do you get materials? We get them from our suppliers. So you can go up to the source of the material, where it came from.
In this case, if we find the source of the material which Bhagavan used to create this Jagat, you can always say that Bhagavan found the material from X. Then X becomes greater than the Bhagawan who created it. Go to X and say, Where did you get the material? From Y. Then Y becomes greater than X because he had the original material.
Ask Y, Where did you get the material? Z had the material, and then Z becomes greater than Y. So this exercise is futile because we cannot get to the ultimate source of the material. You have to come to the conclusion that Bhagavan himself was the source of the material.
In Bhagawan, theres only one thing which he did not have to buy, borrow, or steal , that is his own self. Everything we acquire in this world, we bought from somebody, borrowed from somebody, or took from somebody. But one thing I never had to acquire: that is my own self.
That which I call I. I did not acquire it from anywhere. I didnt buy from anywhere.
So thats the only material available to Bhagavan. So he created this Jagat using his knowledge of creating this universe as an efficient cause. And he also used the material available to him with his own self.
So he became the material cause and the efficient cause for this universe. Therefore he said, everything proceeds from me and I am the source of all things. However, that is not something for us to easily understand.
So give me some examples of glories. It may be difficult to find glory in something which is average. But we can find in something which is really excellent.
If you have a water jug and if you just a little salt in it and you taste it you wont know that there is salt in it. But theres a lot of salt in it. And you taste it, you know theres salt in it.
The Bhagawan has been giving several prominent examples. Sarjanam, Adihicha, Antacha, Madhyamcha Evam, Aham, Arjunah. In the creation for anything which is created and the beginning, the middle and the end, there is no other material to create anything, to sustain anything or destroy anything.
The same material which was used to create this Jagat, everything in Jagat in this universe is also created by the same original material. So Bhagawan said, any creation you see in this world, I am the beginning, the middle and the end. In verse 33 he says, Aksaranam Akaro Asmi.
In previous verse he said, in all the sounds and then one syllable, Om. Because Om is the primordial sound. That is the sound which is the most basic sound out of which all the other variation of sounds come into existence.
As I said, its like three color printing. There are only three cartridges in your printer. But when you print a picture, permutation combination of those three colors created this wonderful picture which is a variety of colors.
So this aa and M is like the source of all the sounds that we hear in this world is the sum total of all the sounds. The Om out of which the first sound is a. U in Ma signifies creation, O signifies such stance and Ma signifies.
So when you close your mouth, its a ma. I heard Anup Jilotra telling a joke. He was teaching a female student.
He said, she will do saregami when it comes to maa, she will skip this ma. He said, why are you skipping Ma? He said, ma, I have to close my mouth so my lipstick gets spoiled. So Ma, you are closing your lips signifying the destruction.
Aa comes from your belly. So thats a creation. Aksaranam akaru asmi.
Among the letters I am a. Every language, the Alphabet starts with A and without a vowel you cannot make any word. And in Sanskrit there is a preponderance of a sound.
Therefore it is so sweet sounding language. Among the compound words in Sanskrit, Im Dwandva. Those of us who have learned a little bit of Sanskrit, there are several compounding words.
I know only one very well. Bahubri samas, yasyakantaha nilaha, Sahneela Kantaha whose neck is blue and Neela kanta, thats a Bahuri samas. So two words, Neela and Kanta, when you combine it With Rajan Kant.
Thats why I remember from my 8th standard Sanskrit that is called Bahu Brahi Samas. Neela is actually almost like an adjective. It does not have same value as Kantha.
Nila is just the attributes of that Kanta. But as Dvanga samas used two words, they both retain their own identity. Dita, Ram, Sita and Ram both maintain their own identity, their own importance.
Therefore Dhvandva is considered the most prominent samas. Bhagavan says among the compound words I am Dhvandva that which retains the value of both. Some commentators have commented that it also may be indicating the self and non self.
So this entire world of ours is made up of something which we call it self that is me and something which is not me, which is non self. In Vedanta, this body, mind, intellect are non self. They are not really permanent.
I am permanent, I feeling is permanent. This beautiful combination of self and non self which we see in our Jagat where self remains the self and still non self retains its own identity as a plurality in this world. So therefore it says Dwandva amongst compound words.
Im Dwandva Aham Eva Akshayaha Kalaha. I am that ever existing time. For he said among the reckoners, Kalaitam kalaham among the measures, I am time.
Everything we know is defined in space and time. Indian philosophers have given more importance to time. They say time is fundamental.
Space is an emergent quality of time. So in that he said, I am the time. Among all the reckon how we measure things, I am time.
In all the measurement, time is the most important one. He said I am that infinite time. It seems like to us it is flowing and going.
But time remains constant. Its our experiences change. Our time starts with the experience of any event followed by the second event.
If theres only one event, there is no time. The first event occurs, there is no time. We measure time between the two events.
Therefore, the measure of time in English is second, not first. There is no time second. So here he says I am that infinite time, not that perceived through your senses as finite time.
Dhata aham Vishwato Mukaha and I am also the Karma Falada. I am also the supporter, the dispenser of all your experiences. I experience as long as IM alive as long as Im conscious.
So my consciousness is the dispenser of all my thoughts and experiences. Daata Viswato Mukaha Facing everywhere that self which in me. Facing everywhere and getting experience of everything is the same self in you.
Facing everywhere, gaining all the experience outside. So when you put it together, Bhagavan is everywhere. No matter where you see, he is there.
Next verse says mrtyuhu Sarva harascha. I am death among all that takes things away from you. You can lose things in some accident.
You can lose things by losing something. Various ways we lose things in life. We lose money in stock market.
But you see that still you will be left with something. I may lose money, but Ill have my health. Im out of health, but Im still alive.
So theres something left. You know, I lost something, but when I die, I lost everything. Theres nothing left for me.
Therefore, once I am the death, it takes away everything from you. You cannot take anything with you. Therefore its a Mrityo Sarva Haraschaham, the greatest taker to take everything that you think is yours.
Udbhavastcha Bhavish. The translation in the book is slightly confusing which says, I am the prosperity of those who are to be prosperous. s not the really appropriate interpretation of Udbhava. Udbhava means to come into existence.
I am the source of all that is coming to be in existence in future. Not only I am the source of all things and beings in present that you see, but I am also the source of everything that will come in existence in future. In other words, past, present and future are just concepts of my mind.
There is only one existence and it exists all the time. And therefore anything which is created in that existence is nothing but the expression of the same supreme reality which is all pervading, everlasting, omnipresent, omniscient, Kirtihi Sri wakcha, NRI nam smruti medha, dhrutikshamah. All women can take some pride here.
All the good qualities are feminine. It says that I am the feminine qualities. Fame, prosperity, speech, memory, intelligence, firmness and forgiveness.
All these qualities are manifest in people because of my presence.

Here Krishna makes His most challenging identification: Mrityuh sarva-harash cha aham - I am death, the all-devouring. Death takes everything we think is ours; nothing survives its grasp. Yet even this ultimate loss is divine manifestation. Why? Because death reveals what is truly ours (consciousness, which survives) versus what was only borrowed (body, possessions, relationships). The all-devouring one is also the great teacher of impermanence and detachment.
Equally striking are the feminine qualities Krishna claims as His own: Kirti (fame), Sri (prosperity), Vak (speech), Smriti (memory), Medha (intelligence), Dhriti (firmness), and Kshama (forgiveness). All these are grammatically feminine in Sanskrit, and Krishna says these positive qualities manifest in people because of His presence. This teaching dignifies the feminine principle - the qualities that nurture, remember, articulate, persist, and pardon are divine signatures. Wherever you see these qualities - in any person of any gender - you see the Lord.
Today, contemplate your relationship with death and loss. Rather than avoiding the thought, recognize: every moment something dies - a breath, an experience, a version of yourself. Can you see this continuous dying as divine teaching, constantly showing you what is essential versus what is passing? And notice the feminine qualities - in yourself, in others, in the world. When someone speaks wisdom, demonstrates memory, shows intelligence or forgiveness - these are not merely personal virtues but manifestations of the divine feminine. Ask: How does my relationship with impermanence change if I see death as divine teacher rather than enemy? Which feminine qualities do I most need to cultivate?
